description: A creeping, mat-forming perennial grass with slender jointed stolons that root at the nodes, short flat grey-green blades, and fingerlike spikes of 3-7 radiating spikelets. It spreads rapidly and is a common lawn and wayside grass.
cultural_significance: Durva is offered with 21 blades to Lord Ganesha and is used in many Hindu rites. It appears in Vedic literature and is regarded as a symbol of life and renewal. Its Vedic prominence is moderate: durva is mentioned in the Atharvaveda and in Vedic ritual texts, while the Ganesha offering is a later Puranic practice.
habitat: Sunny, open ground, lawns, roadsides and fields; thrives in a wide range of soils and warm climates across the tropics.

uses.title: Bleeding disorders (epistaxis, piles)
uses.detail: Fresh juice is traditionally used for nosebleed and bleeding piles; described as Raktastambhaka and Pittahara.

uses.title: Skin diseases and itching
uses.detail: Fresh paste is traditionally applied to rashes, wounds and itching (Kushthaghna).

uses.title: Urinary complaints
uses.detail: Juice or decoction is traditionally used for burning urination (Mutrala).

uses.title: Heat and burning sensation
uses.detail: A cooling drink of fresh juice is a folk remedy for body heat.

uses.title: Antioxidant and glucose research
uses.detail: Laboratory and animal studies suggest antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and blood-sugar effects; human evidence is limited.

ayurveda.vedic_note: Durva (Cynodon dactylon) is mentioned in the Atharvaveda and appears in Vedic ritual contexts as a sacred, life-giving grass. It is more prominent in later ritual (Ganesha puja) than in early hymns, and I am not citing specific verse numbers.

preparations.name: Durva swarasa (fresh juice)
preparations.method: Wash fresh grass and press out the juice.
preparations.note: Traditionally used for nosebleed and body heat; fresh preparation only.

preparations.name: Durva lepa (paste)
preparations.method: Grind fresh blades with water into a paste.

preparations.name: Durvadi ghrita
preparations.method: Classical medicated ghee made with durva.
preparations.note: Traditionally used for bleeding disorders, made by manufacturers.

preparations.name: Durva kwatha
preparations.method: Boil the whole plant in water and strain.
preparations.note: Used by practitioners for urinary complaints.

precautions: Collect only from clean, pesticide-free areas. Pollen is a common cause of hay fever and asthma, and skin contact can cause irritation in sensitive people. May affect blood sugar, so diabetes patients should be cautious. Avoid medicinal amounts in pregnancy without advice.

cultivation.climate: Warm, tolerates a wide range of climates
cultivation.soil: Almost any soil; best in well-drained loam
cultivation.harvest: Cut fresh when needed; regrows quickly

conservation_status: Not threatened; a widespread, often invasive weed.
fun_fact: Because every node can root, a single stolon fragment can start a new plant, which is why durva is hard to remove from fields.

regions.name: South Asia (Widely cultivated)
regions.note: Found everywhere as lawns and wayside grass
